**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The Agreement contains no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on us:

- **§ 2(a) (p0022)** grants a *non-exclusive* licence and goes further than the playbook's preferred position by affirmatively confirming we are "not obligated to utilize the License and [are] free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system... to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink" — subject only to TrueLink's IP rights and our § 10 confidentiality obligations.
- **§ 8 (Client covenants)** contains no sole-source, requirements, or "shall not procure from any third party" language.
- The only exclusivity-flavoured grant runs in our favour's direction of no restriction: **§ 8(d)** is a *non-exclusive* licence from us to TrueLink in Credit Data (subject to the separate Non-Competition Agreement), which does not restrict our sourcing.

Noted in the rationale but not flagged: **§ 3(i) (p0042)** requires us to order a TrueLink credit report on each borrower for which underwriting approval is requested *through a System using the Interface*. This is a narrow, channel-tied service requirement rather than an exclusive-dealing covenant — § 2(a) preserves our freedom to underwrite outside the Interface with other providers — so it does not engage the rule. Worth confirming commercially that credit-report pricing is competitive, since within that channel TrueLink is the only source.
